angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 483,511 km at 16.33 pc = 0.4 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 61.2271 +/- 0.0150 mas (same row, RUWE 0.90): 16.33 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.695 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Dragomir et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 21749 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019ApJ...875L...7D/abstract): 483,511 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.73 +/- 0.07 solar masses from Dragomir et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 21749 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019ApJ...875L...7D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4640 +/- 100 K from Dragomir et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 21749 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019ApJ...875L...7D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Dragomir et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 21749 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019ApJ...875L...7D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gj-143.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.617, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 143 (pscomppars): spectral type K4.5, from Dragomir et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019ApJ...875L...7D/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 143 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.003 dex, from Dragomir et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019ApJ...875L...7D/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 143 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.6862, from Dragomir et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019ApJ...875L...7D/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 143 (pscomppars): age 3.8 Gyr, from Dragomir et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019ApJ...875L...7D/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, HD 21749: projected rotation speed 2.1 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2025A&A...697A.102T)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
